After a run, `show_all_results()` shows three views, in the order you ask
about a run: **is it trustworthy** (which run, did it converge), **what physics
came out**, and **what it cost**. This page is the reference of what each view
shows. [Convergence and reports](../../guides/convergence-and-reports.qmd) is
the task page: it declares convergence, runs, and reads a real report.

## The three views {#common-envelope}

A resolved Palace run (`ResolvedPalaceResult`) has one call per view:

| Call | Shows |
|---|---|
| `show_run_trustworthiness()` | Which run it is and whether it converged: the trust report, [below](#declared-convergence) |
| `show_physics_quantities()` | The capacitance matrix, the mode frequencies or the S-parameters, and Surface EPR |
| `show_simulation_benchmark()` | The time and size of each pass, or of a Driven run's solves |
| `show_all_results()` | All three, in this order |

A resolved AEDT run (`ResolvedRun`) has `show_all_results()`, in the order
identity (project, setup, requested modes, the last pass and whether it
completed), numerical evidence, benchmark, physics and details, and
`show_simulation_benchmark()` on its own
([AEDT time and memory](aedt-runtime.qmd#native-simulation-benchmark)).

Every view takes `theme="light"` (the default) or `theme="dark"` for its
figures, and `show_all_results(theme=...)` passes it on. `show_details=True`
opens the full run record (the receipt, the artifact hashes and the long
tables) and changes nothing in what is selected. It is taken by
`show_all_results`, `show_run_trustworthiness` and `show_simulation_benchmark`
of a Palace run, and by `show_all_results` and `show_simulation_benchmark` of
an AEDT run; `show_physics_quantities` and `inspect_run_trustworthiness` do
not take it. For the full details of a run, call
`show_all_results(show_details=True)`.
Without Plotly the tables are still shown, and each missing plot is named.

`resolve_palace_result(run_dir, expected_handoff_id=...)` reads only a run
that completed and whose files match its handoff and receipt. For a run that
failed or came back in part, use `inspect_run_trustworthiness(run_dir)`: it
shows what the folder holds and keeps the run's recorded state, so an
incomplete run is never shown as complete.

## The trust report {#declared-convergence}

This is the view you open to place a Palace run and judge its convergence. It
shows, in order:

1. **Run Identity**: the problem, the route, the profile, the passes recorded,
   and the MPI and OpenMP counts. A run that is not complete says so here; a
   failed run adds a notice with its category.
2. **Convergence**, when the simulation [declared](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-declaration)
   its criteria: one table laid out as AEDT's convergence table. A row is a
   pass, with its solved elements. A column is a criterion, headed by its name
   and threshold (`C diagonal`, `≤ 0.5 %`), so each number is read against the
   threshold above it; a cell holds the criterion's number at that pass and
   whether it holds (`N/A` for a change at pass 1, which has nothing to compare
   with). Surface-EPR criteria at one inset stand together under the inset's
   name, `Surface EPR, inset 0.5 um` over `MA`, `MS` and `SA`: the part of the
   surfaces 0.5 µm or more from a gap edge. The last column counts the passes
   in a row at which every criterion held.
3. **Each quantity against the pass**, then its declared change on a log axis
   with the threshold as a dashed line. A change carries the name AEDT gives
   it: `Delta %` for a capacitance, `Max Delta Freq. %` for a mode frequency,
   `Max Percent Delta` for a participation. The error-indicator figure carries
   the declared `ErrorIndicator` threshold, or Palace's `Tol` when nothing is
   declared.
4. **Surface EPR Convergence**: for each mode or excitation, one figure per
   interface type, since their participations differ by orders of magnitude,
   with a line for the whole surfaces and one for each inset; then the
   declared changes.

A pass is one Palace solve: pass 1 solves the input mesh. A change is measured
only between two passes read one after the other. How result reading decides
which folder of `results/palace` holds which pass is in
[the internals](../../contribute/internals/report-records.qmd#pass-folders).

With `show_run_trustworthiness(show_details=True)`, or
`show_all_results(show_details=True)`, the report also states the verdict as a
sentence above the table. For a run [stopped at convergence](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-stop)
it reads, for example:

> Converged at pass 4, of the 4 passes read (passes 1 to 4): every criterion
> held at passes 3 to 4, 2 in a row. Last to hold: C diagonal, from pass 3. No
> pass was read after it. SCGSim stopped Palace after pass 4: 2 of the 6 passes
> its limit allows were not run.

A run that did not converge says which criterion fails at the last pass read,
its worst number, the threshold and how many times the threshold that is, and
ends: "Palace ended by itself at its limit of 6 passes." A stopped run has no
final solve of its own: its result, benchmark and cost are those of its last
pass. A stop that did not complete is a failed run, with the failure category
`convergence_stop`. `ResolvedPalaceResult.convergence` holds the same verdict
for a program.

For a run that came back in part, `inspect_run_trustworthiness()` shows the
same table for the passes the folder holds, and the verdict counts the passes
read, for example "3 passes read (passes 1, 4 and 5)".

## A Driven run {#driven-run}

A resolved Palace Driven run (S-parameters, from `DrivenSim`) has the same
calls. Its trust and physics views are a `DrivenTrustReport` and a
`DrivenPhysicsReport`; its benchmark is the shared one.

`show_run_trustworthiness()` shows, in order:

1. **Run Identity**: the same five cards, and the notice of a failed run.
2. **Convergence**: the sweep, each of its ranges and, for more than one,
   the number of frequencies they merge into (`2–10 GHz, 81 points`;
   `4–9 GHz, 501 points; 7.3–7.34 GHz, 4,001 points; 4,497 frequencies`;
   a range of full solves ends in `, full solve`: `7.3566 GHz, full solve`),
   the sampling (`uniform`, or `adaptive, tolerance 0.001` with its cap when
   one is set), the FEM order, the mesh elements and the declared convergence, which is
   `not declared`: a Driven run declares none yet. For an adaptive sweep, a
   table gives each port's samples (the full solves its reduced model was
   built from), the model's estimated error, headed by the tolerance
   (`Estimated error ≤ 0.001`), and the frequencies it solved at, in the
   order Palace added them. A run whose adaptive sweep reached its maximum
   number of samples for a port is still reported: the reason is under
   **Not read**, and no S-parameters are drawn.
3. **Reciprocity and passivity**, recorded and not judged. The reciprocity
   error is the largest `|Sij − Sji|` over every pair of ports and every
   frequency; a network without magnetized or active parts has none. The
   largest singular value of S over the frequencies is at most 1 for a
   passive network. A one-port run has only the second, under **Passivity**.

`show_physics_quantities()` shows the ports in the S-matrix's order, each with
its name in the plan and its impedance; |S| in dB against frequency in two
figures, **Reflection** (`S11`, `S22`) apart from **Transmission** (`S21`,
`S12`), since a matched line reflects at about −40 dB and transmits at about
−0.001 dB; and the **Phase** of every entry in degrees. An entry takes its
excited port's line style, so `S12` is dashed over `S21` where a reciprocal
network draws them on top of each other. Then **Surface EPR**: one figure per
interface type, MA, MS and SA, its participation against frequency. With two
ports or more, each driven port is a group of lines: the whole surfaces, and
one line for each inset. No T1 and no device Q is derived: a driven
participation is the share of the electric energy at one frequency with one
port driven.

`show_simulation_benchmark()` shows the full solves (Palace's linear solves,
one per excited port and solved frequency: every frequency of a uniform
sweep, the samples of an adaptive one), the total wall time and the wall time
per solve, the peak node and rank memory, the degrees of freedom, the mesh
elements and the MPI and OpenMP counts; then the mesh and Palace's timers.

`inspect_run_trustworthiness(run_dir)` reads a returned Driven folder as it
came back, complete or partial: its identity, its failure, its sweep and its
cost. Only a resolved run's S-parameters are read and drawn.

## Physics quantities {#physics-quantities}

Each quantity stays the solver's, with its own units, conductor or port order
and failure meaning: an electrostatic capacitance matrix, mode frequencies, a
driven network response, field-energy participation, a Q3D matrix and Q2D
per-unit-length values are not interchangeable.

### Surface EPR {#eigenmode-epr-presentation}

`show_epr(result, mode=...)` returns a Plotly figure of one mode of an existing
result; it reads no files and starts no solver. For an AEDT adaptive-history
result (`ResolvedRun.epr_result()`), `native_pass=` also picks the pass; a
saved-field result from `analyze_epr` has one evaluation per mode, so `mode=`
is its only selection. It shows surface and bulk participation apart.
AEDT shows a junction's inductive and capacitive participation together on a
junction axis; Palace shows its signed native port participation, which
depends on the phase convention and is not AEDT's pair. Each surface bar names
its owner, its interface and whether it is the whole surface or a margin; the
hover text keeps the source members, the field side and the loss assumptions.
The colours are fixed per interface: MA, MS and SA.

In the integrated AEDT report, each requested mode at the last pass has a
ranking of surface owners, separate bulk and junction plots, and a surface
table with owner, interface, margin, participation, loss and inverse-Q.

[]{#palace-margin-rows}**Margin rows are alternatives, not parts.** A margin
row covers the part of a surface beyond that margin, so it overlaps the
whole-surface row and every other margin row of that surface. Read each on its
own and never add them. `show_physics_quantities()` plots the latest margin
participation against the margin for each mode or excitation and interface.
A participation of zero means the native contribution is zero; on its own it
does not show that a region was left out of the geometry.

The inverse-Q subtotal counts only known whole-surface terms. Unknown losses
are counted as unknown and margin rows are not added. The views show the evidence;
they do not claim a total device Q or a lifetime.

When Palace reports an infinite Q for a mode (`+inf` in `eig.csv`), the report
labels it **native-reported infinite Q** and gives no finite Q for it; the
frequency and energies of that mode are shown as usual
([Eigenmode reference](palace-eigenmode.qmd#native-eigenmode-q)).

### Unknown loss is not zero loss {#honesty-rule}

When you give no loss tangent, Palace's configuration still needs a number and
gets `LossTan=0.0`, but SCGSim records the loss tangent as unknown and shows
that inverse-Q contribution as unavailable. A loss tangent you give as `0`
is a known zero and gives a contribution of zero. For example, an MA film with
no `loss_tangent` shows its participation and no inverse-Q; the same film with
`loss_tangent=0` shows an inverse-Q of 0. [Surface EPR](../../concepts/surface-epr.qmd)
explains the loss assumptions, and [Change loss assumptions without
solving](../../guides/offline-loss.qmd) changes them on a finished result.

## Mesh in the report {#palace-mesh-context}

The Palace report shows the run's mesh summary (`mesh_summary()`): the sizing
recipe and its settings, the quality threshold and the lowest element quality
(minSICN, measured on the linear mesh), the node, element and region counts,
the order of the delivered mesh and the edge lengths. The Eigenmode
degree-of-freedom number is an estimate, not Palace's count;
[Tetrahedral mesh quality](mesh-quality.qmd) explains the numbers.

::: {#palace-run-schemas .callout-important title="Palace run folders of older schemas are not read"}
Result reading reads mesh manifest `schema_version` 2, Palace index map
`schema_version` 3 and detached EPR results `scgsim.palace.epr-result.v2`. A
run folder or detached result of an older schema is refused with an error that
names its version. To read such a study again, prepare it with the current
package and run it again.
:::

## What the views do not judge {#research-interpretation-and-retained-observations}

The views report the solver's status and your criteria. Whether a result
answers your research question is your judgement; keep your criteria and any
change to them with the run. [Convergence and reports](../../guides/convergence-and-reports.qmd)
says how to read them for a study.

## Not available {#current-palace-scope}

Palace Magnetostatic reports, a convergence declaration for a Driven run, a
plot of Palace's `domain-E.csv` volume energy, and an export format for a
report.
